_comment: Site registry per docs/03. Deployment records are REQUIRED before project-sensor ingest (docs/06 registry gate). window_local values below are from the reviewed Tidbit deployment; verify before first real run. series_map keys are the sensor name as it appears in the vendor file header ('Tidbit 1 , degF' -> 'Tidbit 1'), not the full column label; values are controlled parameter names from parameters.json. measured_parameters on a public station lists the controlled parameters that station actually carries an instrument for; a fetcher stores only those, so a fixed-column format cannot land rows for a sensor the station does not have. Omit it only while nobody has checked - an absent field means undeclared, and the fetcher stores everything it recognises and says so. site_id and a deployment's depth_m are both part of the storage dedupe key, so both are IMMUTABLE once rows for that deployment have landed in observations/ - editing either leaves the old rows behind under the old key, nothing raises, and one instrument becomes two series (docs/03 'Partition files and idempotence'). Correcting window_local is not in this class and is safe: it moves qc_flag, not the key. sensor_depths_m takes a number when the registry supplies the depth and a LIST when the payload does - a moored string measures one parameter at many depths, so the list records which depths have been seen rather than a value the fetcher writes (docs/03 'A source may be self-describing on depth'). For an ERDDAP-served station, station_code is the pinned dataset ID: it is the identifier the provider knows the station by, which is what a fetcher asks for.

sites.name: TidbiT 1 site (yellow buoy)

deployments.notes: depth_m is the logger depth, reported by the placer as 27 fsw and converted at 0.3048 m/ft. fsw here is feet of depth as a dive computer displays it, not the 1/33 atm pressure unit, which would give 8.27 m.

sites.notes: Position surveyed and supplied by the placer 2026-08-27, superseding the conflicting reports ~1-2 km apart this record previously carried and the null it held while they stood. WGS84, converted from 32 deg 51' 08.2" N, 117 deg 16' 10.1" W. Position is a site fact, not a deployment one: a redeployment of this logger at another spot is a new site record, not another deployments[] entry here.

sites.name: TidbiT 2 site

deployments.notes: series_map key is 'Temperature', the name in this file's column header - the logger's series name was left at the factory default, so it is NOT 'Tidbit 2'. window_local is PROVISIONAL and derived from the record itself, not from a dive log: the first four samples read 21.2-22.2 degC on deck, 07:40 reads 14.8 degC and it stays down, settling only 0.4 degC over the next 20 minutes, so the logger was in and near-equilibrated by 07:40. At the other end there is nothing to exclude - Host Connected and End of File share 08:36:48, so it was stopped the instant it was connected and never warmed; the last sample is 08:30 at 15.6 degC. Confirm against the dive log and correct here: a corrected window is a registry edit plus a rebuild, and excluded rows are flagged (qc_flag 4), never deleted. Do not trust the same derivation on a shallow logger: PROJ:TIDBIT-1's window came from the placer's own hand-edited file, and a first-cold-reading rule would have picked its 07:40 dunk and been wrong by two samples. Cost if this window is wrong by a sample: min/mean/max do not move (13.12/16.50/23.02 degC either way), but threshold and spell features do - all four on-deck rows are >= 20 degC and they set 11 Jul's daily maximum to 22.18 degC where the water reached 20.36 degC. depth_m is the logger depth, reported by the placer as 55 fsw and converted at 0.3048 m/ft; the 1/33 atm pressure definition would give 16.85 m.

sites.notes: Position surveyed and supplied by the placer 2026-08-27. WGS84, as given in decimal degrees. Its own site rather than a second deployments[] entry on PROJ:TIDBIT-1: it sits 455 m from that logger and 8.5 m deeper, and position is a site fact that Deployment cannot carry by construction. Corroborated by the data - over the span the two records share (11 Jul 08:00 to 1 Aug 07:30 local, 3,022 samples each) this logger averaged 17.42 degC against 21.58 degC at PROJ:TIDBIT-1, which is what sitting below the thermocline looks like and is why the two cannot share a record. neighbor_refs names NDBC:LJAC1 and COOPS:9410230 because that platform is the nearest public station, not because it is depth-comparable: its only sea_water_temperature sensor sits 3.4 m below MLLW, 13.4 m above this logger and above the summer thermocline. Over 13 Jul - 1 Aug 2026, where LJAC1's record in observations/ overlaps this deployment, that reference averaged 22.56 degC against this logger's 17.42 degC. Reporting that ~5 degC gap as instrument bias would invert what docs/04's neighbor validation table is evidence for, so bias and RMSE are NOT reportable for this site; correlation is, labelled with the depth gap. PROJ:TIDBIT-1 at 8.23 m does not carry the caveat - the same reference sits 4.8 m above it and the offset there is about 1 degC. See docs/04 'Neighbor validation'.

sites.name: La Jolla shore station (NDBC)
sites.notes: Sensor geometry from the NDBC station page, retrieved 2026-08-25: sea temp depth 3.4 m below MLLW; air temp 7.2 m and anemometer 8.2 m above a site elevation of 9.3 m above MSL. The 3.4 m intake is why depth_m is recorded per parameter - comparing it to a logger at another depth is the error docs/02 says to prevent structurally. NOT an independent station from COOPS:9410230: the NDBC station page titles this platform 'LJAC1 - 9410230 - La Jolla, CA', owned by NOAA NOS. NDBC redistributes the NOS observations, so the two site records describe one instrument package and must never both count as neighbors for the same validation. measured_parameters omits the wave parameters because this shore station has no wave sensor: the stdmet format carries WVHT and DPD in every file, and across the 2007-2025 archive plus realtime all 3,289,004 wave rows are the sentinel, with exactly one distinct value in each column of the landed 2023 file (87,302 records). Wave data for this location comes from CDIP, not from here.

sites.name: La Jolla (Scripps Pier) tide station
sites.notes: Same NOS platform as NDBC:LJAC1 - see that record. Water level here is the product CO-OPS serves with an explicit datum (MLLW, docs/03); NDBC's TIDE column for the same platform declares no datum and is deliberately not ingested.

sites.name: Point Loma Ocean Outfall RTOMS mooring
sites.notes: Position 32.66996, -117.32676 taken from the CeNCOOS ERDDAP dataset and verified 2026-08-28 to be internally consistent: the dataset's geospatial_lat/lon attributes and the latitude/longitude columns of the rows themselves give the same pair, and it agrees with the depth the string reaches - 90 m off a Point Loma outfall terminus at about 94 m. That check is not ceremony: the sibling south-bay-ocean-outfall-historic dataset gives three different answers for where its instrument was, so a position from this provider is corroborated before it is recorded (docs/02 'City of San Diego RTOMS'). The mooring is a watch-circle buoy and its instantaneous position moves with the current; this is the nominal anchor position the provider publishes, not a GPS fix. sensor_depths_m lists the 11 depths carrying sea_water_temperature on this feed, read from the rows where that variable is not null - the dataset's z axis takes far more values than this because it is a TimeSeriesProfile that flattens the ADCP's 1 m velocity bins onto the same axis. 9 m and 10 m are both here and are the same physical position on the string across two deployments; they land as two series rather than being rounded together, because depth_m is part of the storage key and permanent. NOT a neighbor_ref for any project sensor and deliberately absent from every polygon's site_ids: it is 25 km from the La Jolla beds and sits on a wastewater diffuser, so it is a depth reference for docs/04 neighbor validation to reason about, not a nearby station. It also cannot validate the project loggers at all - this record ends 2024-12-09 and their deployments begin July 2026.

sites.name: South Bay Ocean Outfall RTOMS mooring
sites.notes: Position 32.53171, -117.18631, verified on the same basis as SDRTOMS:PLOO on 2026-08-28 - attributes and row columns agree, and the 26 m string depth matches the shallower South Bay outfall. Its 2020-01 to 2022-11 history is NOT ingested: that window lives only in south-bay-ocean-outfall-historic, which claims Point Loma's coordinates in its metadata, La Jolla's in its own latitude/longitude columns, and South Bay's in its depth range. The depths are the only one of the three matching the title, so the data is probably this mooring's and both positions are wrong - but that is a guess, and position is a reviewed fact here, so the window is left out until the provider fixes it (docs/02). Coverage therefore starts 2021-11-03 and runs to 2025-06-04. sensor_depths_m lists the 6 depths carrying sea_water_temperature, read from the non-null rows; 25 m and 26 m, and 18 m and 20 m, are deployment-to-deployment drift on the same positions and land as separate series. Nearest of the two moorings to KELP:IMPERIAL-BEACH, which is why it is worth holding at all, but still ~15 km from it and on a diffuser: not a neighbor_ref, and not in any polygon's site_ids.
